2609.25852.title: Prediction Is Not Detection: Evaluating Pre-Recognition Claims in Longitudinal Clinical AI
2609.25852.paper_summary: Clinically useful early detection requires validated pre-recognition lead time. Yet event-based evaluations of longitudinal clinical AI can treat recognition-mediated care-process signals as shortcuts and recognition-dependent endpoints as reference standards, inflating apparent performance and lead time while undermining cross-center transport. Such results may serve prognosis without establishing detection before recognition. We define an interval-censored pre-recognition transition, an independent as-of reference standard, and a prespecified recognition proxy to make the claim testable.
2609.25852.paper_summary_zh: 臨床上有用的早期檢測需要經過驗證的預認識提前時間。<lb/>然而，基於事件的長期臨床人工智慧評估可以將認識介導的護理過程信號視為捷徑，並將依賴認識的終點視為參考標準，這樣會膨脹表面性能和提前時間，同時削弱跨中心的轉運。<lb/>這樣的結果可能有助於預後，但並未在認識之前建立檢測。<lb/>我們定義了一個區間右截斷的預認識轉變，一個獨立的即時參考標準，以及一個預先指定的認識代理，以使該主張可測試。
